objective_notes: What the candidate describes is mostly what KADS already intends, and each part has clauses behind it. Separation from the author: 1.1 (a), 1.2 (a), 3.5 (a), 6.1 (a), and the Why of proposition 6 ('without its author at hand'). Separation from original context: 1.1 (c), 1.2, 4.3 (a), 6.1 (b) scope, 7.2.6 (a) scoping of negatives. Passage of time: 4.1, 4.2, 4.3, 5.2 (b), 8.3 (b), 8.4. Transformation: 2.2 (a) to (d), 2.4 (a), 5.1 (b), 3.5 (the Agent-drafted term). Skeptical inspection: 3.1 to 3.6, 7.2.3 to 7.2.6, 3.4 (b). Two parts are stronger than the 0.9.0 text guarantees. First, 'a discoverable path from material answers to the basis on which they stand': Core guarantees that a material factual claim has an identifiable basis (3.1 a, 'identifiable', not reachable), that an artifact behind a claim has a discoverable location (3.6 a), and that maintained documents are reachable from the entry point (2.3, a SHOULD); it does not guarantee a path from the answer to the reasoning or the method, because 3.1 (a) names neither, 7.1.5 (c) and 7.2.1 bind only under declared profiles, and 4.3 (b) asks for the method only when it differs from current conditions. The 0.8.0 sentence that stated this path as a SHOULD was removed in 0.9.0 (see regression_evidence). Second, 'preserving' a path is stronger than KADS can promise when the basis was never written down: 3.3 (b), 3.2 (b), 7.1.5 (c, 'state that they are not recorded') and 3.4 (a, 'state which of these is not recorded') show that what KADS actually guarantees is that the basis is reachable or its absence is visible; it cannot preserve what no one recorded, and it rightly forbids inventing it (3.3 a). 'Survive' overstates in the same way: KADS makes a document carry what a reader needs; it does not keep knowledge alive. Missing from the candidate: proposition 2. A reader separated from the author also needs to know which of several descriptions is the authoritative one for their scope (2.1 a, b; 1.2 b; 4.1 d); 'original context' does not cover it, and it is the one invariant the candidate's five hazards do not name. Also missing is the bound that foundations.md states (a rule earns its place only when its absence costs readers more than it costs authors); an objective without it reads as a licence for every traceability rule, which the brief's admission rule and proposition 7 deny. Placement: docs/foundations.md under 'Design constraint', which is the canonical home of 'why KADS is shaped the way it is'; README line 5 already carries a four-item plain-words version and should stay a summary of it (2.2 d, no firmer than its source); it does not belong in the specification preface, where it would be read as a ninth proposition, nor in the knowledge model, which explains concepts rather than aims. It stays informative.
objective_revised: KADS exists so that technical knowledge stays usable and assessable by a reader who arrives without its author, without its original context, and without knowing what has changed since it was written, including after the knowledge has been summarized, generated, or restated. Such a reader can tell what a document is and when it applies; which description is authoritative for their scope and whether it is current; how firmly each material statement is held and what kind of statement it is; and can reach the basis, the reasoning, and the method on which a material answer stands, or see plainly that they were not recorded. KADS asks for this in proportion to the consequence of the knowledge being wrong, and asks nothing that costs authors more than its absence costs readers.
regression_evidence: The cut was recorded, so it was not an oversight in the editing sense, but it rested on a premise that does not hold, and the editors' own accounting shows they believed no guarantee was lost. (1) J-034 row 1.3 says the evidence-path SHOULD was removed as 'a duplicate of 3.1 a and 7.2.1'. 3.1 (a) reads 'Material factual claims MUST have an identifiable basis: relevant code, an authoritative reference, an observation, a derivation, or an explicit assumption awaiting verification'. It covers factual claims, not recommendations or decisions; it asks that the basis be identifiable, not that the path to it be explicit; and it names neither the reasoning from basis to claim nor the method, which were two of the four layers in the removed sentence ('context, reasoning, method, and sources'). 7.2.1 names both but, per the 7.2 lead-in and 8.1 (c), binds only a project that declares the research-report profile. In Core, therefore, the reasoning layer now has no clause at all and the method layer has only 4.3 (b), which triggers only when the method differs from current conditions. (2) J-034's Answer says 0.9.0 'relaxes two requirements (7.2.1 ... 8.4)' and the changelog 0.9.0 entry lists the same two, with migration 'Recommended: nothing'. The 1.3 SHOULD appears only in the counting table as one of seven removed SHOULDs; the Changed section's list of 'explanations ... moved to the clause guide' names 'no fixed sequence of files' and 'learning content exposes prerequisites' but not the evidence path. So the editors classified it as a duplicate, not as a relaxation; had they thought a recommendation was being retired they would have listed it beside 7.2.1. (3) The claimed relocation did not happen. The subtractor's stated new home was 'README (already there as a navigation aid)'; README line 62 says a reader 'may follow the path', which is permission to a reader, not advice to an author. The 0.8.0 clause guide row 1.3 read 'Make it possible to get from the answer to its reasons, method, and sources'; the 0.9.0 row replaced that with 'No fixed sequence of files or headings is required', so guidance lost the sentence at the same time the specification did. The Evidence path term went too. Only authoring-guide line 48 ('Reveal context, reasoning, method, and sources as the reader needs them') and learning-and-terminology line 5 remain, both predating 0.9.0 and neither cited by J-034 as the new home. (4) The J-034 guardian did not contest the duplicate claim; its objection to 1.3 was only that removing both 'No fixed sequence' and the Evidence path term would let a reviewer read the surviving sentence as a prescribed order. The dispositions file (proposed-dispositions.md row 1.3) had proposed keeping the sentence; the subtractor's argument moved it out, and no challenger examined whether 3.1 (a) actually covers reasoning and method. (5) Neither the 0.8.0 nor the 0.9.0 conformance page has a review question for 1.3, so the recommendation was never tested in review and its loss was invisible to the review record. Net: an edit intended as a safe simplification that removed the only Core text, normative or guidance, asking an author to make the reasoning and method behind a material answer reachable. The practical effect is bounded because the sentence was a SHOULD: no corpus changed status; what changed is that an author who leaves the reasoning out no longer owes a stated reason and a reviewer has no clause to cite.

counterexamples.corpus: Core only, three files. README.md: entry point with the adoption note inline (KADS 0.9.0; corpus docs/; profiles: common core; exceptions: none; maintainer: platform team; review on release) and a review record (self-review, 2026-10-01, revision abc123, no unresolved items). docs/connection-pool.md: '# Connection pool size for the order service. For operators of the order service, version 4.x on the shared Postgres cluster. Set pool_size = 8. Observed: benchmark run 2026-09-12-1 measured p95 latency and error rate at pool sizes 4, 8, 16, and 32 on staging, version 4.2; raw table in the run. Decided: 8, by the platform lead on 2026-09-15, effective from release 4.3. Limits: single node, synthetic load, staging only.' docs/runs/2026-09-12-1/README.md: run ID, collection time 2026-09-12 10:00 UTC, environment, a table with units (ms, percent) in which 8 and 16 are within a few milliseconds of each other and 16 has the lower p95. The actual reason for 8 (a cluster-wide connection budget shared with two other services) was discussed in a meeting and never written anywhere.
counterexamples.conforms_by: 1.1 (a) opens with what, question, scope; (b) nothing about the document itself; 1.2 (a) purpose and scope stated, (b) entry point directs to current content; 1.3 answer first; 1.4 no evaluative term; 2.1 (a) one home for the setting; 2.2 no summary present; 2.3 both pages linked from README; 2.4 nothing generated; 3.1 (a) basis is an observation, (b) citation points to the specific run, (c) no uninspected source; 3.2 (a) Observed and Decided are marked and distinct, (b) the claim is supported, (c) the run's limits are disclosed; 3.3 nothing invented; 3.4 no verification claim made; 3.5 not agent-drafted; 3.6 (a) run location, version, role, and interpretation limits stated, (b) no deployed-state claim; 4.1 to 4.3 nothing superseded, date of the measurement given; 5.1 (a) raw table kept, (b) no alteration; 5.2 (a) unique ID, (b) dated directory not reusable, (c) collection time recorded separately; 6.1 (b) units, scope, time, source, aggregation (p95 of N) given; 6.3 (a) links resolve; 8.1 (a) to (e) declared; 8.2 no local rules; 8.4 (a) note pins 0.9.0, no version of its own; 8.5 review recorded. 7.1.5 (c) and 7.2.1 do not bind: no profile declared.
counterexamples.fails_reader_because: The reader who must decide whether 8 still holds for version 5 can reach the answer and the evidence but not the reasoning from the evidence to the answer. The table mildly favours 16; the page says 8 was decided. Nothing says whether 8 was chosen from the data, in spite of it, or on a constraint the data does not show, and nothing says that the reason is unrecorded. A skeptical reader cannot tell why the conclusion deserves confidence and cannot tell what would change it.
counterexamples.caught_in_0_8_0_by: 1.3 sentence 2: 'The evidence path from answer to context, reasoning, method, and sources SHOULD be explicit where those layers are relevant.' The reasoning layer is relevant (the answer is a chosen value, not a read-off), it is not explicit, and no reason for the departure is given, which the keywords paragraph requires ('the reason belongs with the departure'). A 0.8.0 reviewer could cite 1.3 and ask either for the reason or for 'reason not recorded'. The 0.8.0 clause-guide row 1.3 ('Make it possible to get from the answer to its reasons, method, and sources') said the same in plain words. Under 0.9.0 the reviewer has nothing to cite: 3.1 (a) is satisfied by the observation, 3.2 (b) by the citation, and 7.1.5 (c) is out of scope.
counterexamples.closed_by: Add to clause 3.1 a lettered item (d), keyword SHOULD: '(d) Where a material claim rests on reasoning or a method that the document does not itself contain, the document SHOULD say where that reasoning or method is recorded, or that it is not recorded.' Clause 3.1 is the right carrier because the gap is in what counts as support, not in the order of a page; a 1.3 (b) with the same words is the fallback if the editors prefer the historical location. Add the matching review question to conformance.md under Common core: 'Where a material answer rests on reasoning or a method kept elsewhere, can the reader reach it, or is it stated that it was not recorded?' (3.1).
counterexamples.burden: On a ten-line how-to whose answer is the procedure itself (stop, run, confirm), the condition is not met and nothing is owed. On a ten-line how-to that fixes a value or a choice, one parenthetical: '(why 8: see connection-pool.md)' or '(reason not recorded)'. No new file, section, term, or identifier.

counterexamples.corpus: Core only, three files. README.md as in the first corpus. docs/worker-cold-start.md: '# Worker cold-start time. For capacity planners of the batch worker, version 5.1, staging cluster. Observed: cold start is 1.9 s at p50 and 3.4 s at p95 (200 starts, 2026-09-29, staging, worker 5.1; raw timings in run 2026-09-29-1). Not measured on production.' docs/runs/2026-09-29-1/README.md: run ID, collection time, environment, a CSV of 200 timings in seconds, and the sentence 'Collected by the author on 2026-09-29.' Nowhere does any page say what 'cold start' was measured between: process spawn to first health-check response, to first job dequeued, or to first job completed, nor whether the image was warm on the node.
counterexamples.conforms_by: 1.1, 1.2, 1.3 as before; 2.1 (a) one home; 2.3 reachable; 3.1 (a) basis is an observation, (b) the citation points to the specific run; 3.2 (a) marked Observed, (b) supported, (c) the known limitation (staging only) is disclosed; 3.3 nothing invented, the unmeasured case is stated; 3.4 no verification claim; 3.6 (a) location, version, role (observation), interpretation limit (staging, not production) discoverable; 4.3 (a) the date is given, (b) not triggered: nothing about the method 'differ[s] from current ones' because no method was ever recorded against which a difference could be seen; 5.1 (a) timings kept raw; 5.2 (a) to (c) satisfied; 6.1 (b) units (s), scope (staging, 5.1), time, source, and aggregation (p50, p95 of 200) all exposed; 6.3 (a) links resolve; 8.1, 8.4 (a), 8.5 as before. 7.2.2 (a), which would require enough of the method for a reader to attempt it, does not bind: no research-report profile declared, and a capacity page is not a report.
counterexamples.fails_reader_because: A planner who measures 3.5 s on their own cluster cannot tell whether that contradicts the page, because the page's figure has no reachable method. Every number carries units, scope, date, and source, so every quantity clause passes; what the reader cannot reach is how the number was produced, which decides whether it is comparable to anything. The answer is clear and the method is unreachable.
counterexamples.caught_in_0_8_0_by: 1.3 sentence 2, the method layer: relevant (a timing figure depends on its endpoints), not explicit, no departure stated. Also partially by 0.8.0 6.1 'Research claims MUST state limitations relevant to their interpretation', if a reviewer read a measured figure on a planning page as a research claim; 0.9.0 removed that sentence as a duplicate of 3.2 (c), which only covers known limitations and does not reach an unstated method. Under 0.9.0 the reviewer can cite nothing: 4.3 (b) needs a recorded method to compare with, 7.2.2 is out of scope.
counterexamples.closed_by: The same 3.1 (d) as above; the words 'or a method' are what this corpus needs. Under it the page says either 'cold start measured from process spawn to first 200 from /health' or 'measurement endpoints not recorded', and the planner knows which. A secondary fix that is not a rule: the clause-guide row 4.3 should say that (b) presumes the method was recorded somewhere, so that authors see why 3.1 (d) matters for a fact that may later change.
counterexamples.burden: A ten-line how-to that reports no measured figure owes nothing. One that does owes one clause of one sentence naming what was measured between, or 'method not recorded'. This is already the practice the README example shows for 'Verified' (3.4 a); the rule extends the same habit from verification claims to measured figures.

counterexamples.corpus: Core only, four files. README.md as before. docs/troubleshooting/importer-stalls.md: '# Importer stalls after a slow upstream. For operators of the importer, version 2.x. Recommended: raise batch_timeout to 120 s. Sources: incident INC-442 post-mortem (docs/incidents/INC-442.md); batch_timeout in the configuration reference (docs/reference/importer-config.md#batch_timeout); run 2026-08-03-1 (docs/runs/2026-08-03-1/README.md).' INC-442.md: a dated post-mortem concluding that the stall was caused by an upstream that answered in 70 to 95 s during the incident window. importer-config.md: defines batch_timeout, default 60 s, range 10 to 600 s. Run 2026-08-03-1: importer logs from the incident showing timeouts at 60 s. All three sources are genuine, inspected, and resolve. No page says why 120 s rather than 100 s or 300 s, nor whether 120 s was ever tried.
counterexamples.conforms_by: 1.1 (a) the page says what it is and for whom; 1.3 the answer is first; 2.1 (a) the setting's home is the reference page and this page does not restate the definition; 2.2 (d) the incident's finding is restated no more firmly than the post-mortem; 2.3 all pages reachable; 3.1 (a) the material claim has identifiable bases of three listed kinds (an observation in the run, an authoritative reference, and a dated finding), (b) each citation points to the specific artifact or anchor, (c) nothing uninspected; 3.2 (a) 'Recommended' is marked and distinct from the observations, (b) the claim is not unsupported, it is cited, (c) no known contradiction; 3.3 nothing invented; 3.4 no verification claim is made, and none is required; 3.6 (a) the run's location, period, role, and limits are discoverable on the run page; 4.3 (a) the incident and the run are dated; 5.1, 5.2 satisfied by the run; 6.1 (a) the action, the prerequisite (version 2.x), and a completion condition ('the importer resumes within one batch') are stated; 6.3 (a) all links resolve; 8.1, 8.4 (a), 8.5 as before. 7.2.1 does not bind: not a report, no profile declared.
counterexamples.fails_reader_because: Every claim has a citation and every citation resolves, but the inference that joins them to the number 120 cannot be found. The post-mortem gives a range; the reference gives the bounds; the run shows the failure at 60 s. Whether 120 was computed (largest observed plus margin), tried, or guessed is nowhere, and no page says so. The relation of the evidence to the conclusion is implicit; a skeptical reader can verify every source and still not know whether the recommendation is sound or how to adjust it when the upstream changes.
counterexamples.caught_in_0_8_0_by: 1.3 sentence 2: the reasoning layer is relevant to a figure the operator will apply, it is not explicit, and no departure is stated. In 0.9.0, 3.1 (a) is satisfied by the citations themselves, which is exactly the failure the brief names ('every claim has a citation but evidence-to-conclusion reasoning cannot be found'); 3.2 (b) reads 'unsupported' and this claim is supported in the sense 3.1 defines.
counterexamples.closed_by: 3.1 (d) as proposed. The page then reads 'Recommended: raise batch_timeout to 120 s (largest upstream latency observed in INC-442 plus 25 percent; not yet tried under load)' or '(reasoning for the figure not recorded)'. The first sentence of the proposed rule also closes the derived-view variant: an index that restates '120 s recommended' keeps its standing under 2.2 (d) and inherits the pointer or the 'not recorded' statement as a material qualification under 2.2 (a).
counterexamples.burden: One clause in one sentence on a page that already lists three sources. Nothing on a how-to that recommends no value.

counterexamples.corpus: Core plus the tracked-record profile, five files. README.md as before but declaring the profile and the namespace. decisions/D-012.md: a decision record with ID, type, title, status accepted, updated date; 'Authorized by the engineering director on 2026-09-20, effective 2026-11-01. Decision: the order service moves its queue to Kafka. Reasons: not recorded.' decisions/J-007.md: an investigation record, status complete, comparing Kafka and RabbitMQ for this workload and concluding they are equivalent on every criterion measured; it carries no relationship to D-012 and D-012 carries none to it. docs/queue-client.md: a how-to that says 'Use the Kafka client (decided in D-012)'. The real reason (an existing vendor contract) was never written anywhere.
counterexamples.conforms_by: 7.1.1 all five fields once; 7.1.2 (a) IDs unique and stable, (c) nomenclature types; 7.1.3 the one stated relationship (the how-to's 'decided in') has an explicit meaning and resolves, and the clause binds only relationships that are stated, not ones that are missing; 7.1.4 nothing superseded; 7.1.5 (a) status is lifecycle, (b) no certainty claim is mixed into it, (c) authority and effective date are given and the SHOULD is satisfied by its third option, 'state that they are not recorded', which is a true statement; 3.3 (a) nothing invented, which is exactly why the reasons are not supplied; 3.2 (a) Decided is marked; 2.3 both records reachable from the index; 6.3 links resolve; 8.1 (c) the profile is declared. Not a research report, so 7.2 does not bind J-007 unless the project declares it, and the corpus does not.
counterexamples.fails_reader_because: The reader of the how-to who wants to know whether the decision still holds after the contract ends can reach the decision and learn only that its reasons are unrecorded; they cannot know that J-007 exists, that it found no technical difference, or that the real ground was commercial. The decision records authorization but no reconstructable rationale.
counterexamples.caught_in_0_8_0_by: Honestly, not prevented in 0.8.0 either. 0.8.0 7.1.5 contained the same 'or state that they are not recorded' option, and 0.8.0 1.3 sentence 2 was a SHOULD whose departure 'reasons were never written' is itself a stated reason. This corpus marks the limit of what KADS can guarantee, in either version: when the basis was never recorded, KADS guarantees only that the absence is visible, and 3.3 (a) rightly forbids inventing it. The corpus is included because the brief asks for it and because it bounds the objective (see objective_notes): 'preserving a discoverable path' is stronger than 'reach the basis or see that it was not recorded'. The part that 3.1 (d) would still improve: J-007 is a reachable record that bears on D-012, and 3.1 (d) applied to the how-to or the decision would prompt 'related investigation: J-007' beside 'reasons not recorded', since that reasoning is recorded, even if the final ground is not. Whether a missing material relationship between two existing records is a 7.1.3 violation is itself a finding: 7.1.3 reads only on stated relationships.
counterexamples.closed_by: Not closable by a rule without violating 3.3 (a) or forcing invented rationale; the honest outcome is the one the corpus has. The partial improvement is 3.1 (d) as proposed, which makes the author say 'not recorded' at the point of use in the how-to rather than only inside the decision record, and point at J-007 where it exists. No change to 7.1.5 (c) is proposed; its third option is correct.
counterexamples.burden: None beyond what 7.1.5 (c) already asks of a decision record. On a ten-line how-to that cites a decision: nothing, or 'reason: see D-012' which it already says.

proposed_rule.text: (d) Where a material claim rests on reasoning or a method that the document does not itself contain, the document SHOULD say where that reasoning or method is recorded, or that it is not recorded.
proposed_rule.placement: Clause 3.1, A basis for every material claim (author), as a new lettered item (d) after (c). Rationale for the carrier: 3.1 is the clause whose scope J-034 said already covered this, and the new item makes the non-duplication explicit by naming the two layers 3.1 (a) does not (reasoning, method) while reusing the 'or that it is not recorded' form of 3.4 (a) and 7.1.5 (c). Fallback placement if the editors prefer the historical home: clause 1.3 as item (b), with 1.3 relettered (a) for the answer-first sentence. In either case add one review question to docs/conformance.md Common core: 'Where a material answer rests on reasoning or a method kept elsewhere, can the reader reach it, or is it stated that it was not recorded?' citing the clause, and restore the plain-words sentence to the clause-guide row: 'Make it possible to get from the answer to its reasons and method, or say they were not recorded.' Do not reintroduce the Evidence path term or the five-step label; neither is needed to read the sentence.

admission.not_already_protected: 3.1 (a) requires an identifiable basis of five listed kinds for material factual claims; it names neither the reasoning from basis to claim nor the method, and 'identifiable' is weaker than reachable. 3.1 (b) is a SHOULD about where a citation points, not whether the reasoning exists. 3.2 (b) marks unsupported claims, but a claim with resolving citations and no reasoning is supported in 3.1's sense (corpus 3). 3.2 (c) covers known contradictions and limitations, not an unstated method. 3.6 (a) covers artifacts, not reasoning. 4.3 (b) asks for the method only where it differs from current conditions, which cannot be seen if it was never recorded (corpus 2). 2.3 and 6.3 govern whether documents are reachable and links resolve, not whether a link to the reasoning exists. 7.1.5 (c), 7.2.1, and 7.2.2 bind only under a declared profile. Neither the 0.8.0 nor the 0.9.0 conformance page has a review question for the removed 1.3 sentence, so nothing in the normative review instrument protects it. Guidance: the 0.9.0 clause-guide row 1.3 dropped the only plain-words statement; authoring-guide line 48 and README line 62 remain, both informative and both predating the cut.
admission.conforming_violation: Corpora 1 to 3 above conform to every 0.9.0 clause that binds them, cited item by item, and in each a skeptical reader cannot reach the reasoning (1, 3) or the method (2) behind a material answer and is not told that it is unrecorded. Corpus 3 is the brief's 'every claim has a citation but evidence-to-conclusion reasoning cannot be found' case; corpus 2 is 'the answer is clear but the method is unreachable'; corpus 1 is 'every requirement passes but the reader cannot tell why a material conclusion deserves confidence'.
admission.small_and_testable: One sentence, one requirement, one keyword. Detection by reading one page (Contributing question 5): the reasoning or method is on the page, pointed to, or declared unrecorded; a departure from the SHOULD carries its reason. It adds no term, no clause number, no profile, no identifier, no section. Restoring a SHOULD that 0.8.0 carried is not breaking under 8.3 (c); it is a minor change under 8.3 (e) and returns a conformant 0.8.0 corpus to exactly its prior obligations. Cost on upgrade day for an existing conformant corpus: nothing, since a SHOULD changes no status; an author who had omitted the reasoning owes the reason for the omission or the words 'not recorded', as under 0.8.0.
admission.guidance_insufficient: Guidance already existed in 0.8.0 (authoring guide line 48, README line 62, clause-guide row 1.3) alongside the SHOULD, and guidance alone is what 0.9.0 left; the corpora above are built against that guidance and pass review because a reviewer applying conformance.md has no question to ask and no clause to cite. The property at stake is the one proposition 3 exists for ('A claim is no stronger than its support'; Why: 'A reader acts on what a document says'), and the brief's admission rule says a foundational guarantee is not removed because fewer words are possible. The README's promise at line 5 ('where each important claim comes from') and line 62 (a path 'to an answer and its basis') is, for reasoning and method in Core, currently a promise with no rule behind it; a SHOULD is the smallest text that makes the promise true and that gives a reviewer something to cite.

other_findings.problem: The 0.8.0 row read 'Make it possible to get from the answer to its reasons, method, and sources.' The 0.9.0 row dropped that sentence and kept only 'No fixed sequence of files or headings is required.' J-034 says what left the specification went to the clause guide; for the evidence-path sentence the clause guide lost it at the same time, so the sentence has no home in guidance either.
other_findings.fix: Restore the sentence to the row (in the 3.1 row if 3.1 (d) is adopted): 'Make it possible to get from the answer to its reasons and method, or say they were not recorded.'

other_findings.problem: No review question cites clause 1.3 in 0.9.0, and none did in 0.8.0. The only clause under propositions 1 to 6 and 8 that the review instrument never asks about. Whatever the specification says about the path from answer to basis is therefore untested in review.
other_findings.fix: Add one row: 'Where a material answer rests on reasoning or a method kept elsewhere, can the reader reach it, or is it stated that it was not recorded?' with the clause that carries the rule (3.1 if (d) is adopted). If 1.3 stays as a single sentence, add 'Does the page give the answer before the background?' (1.3) so that every Core clause has a question.

other_findings.location: Disposition table, row 1.3, line 51; Answer, line 17
other_findings.problem: The row records the evidence-path SHOULD as 'a duplicate of 3.1 a and 7.2.1'. 3.1 (a) names neither reasoning nor method and binds factual claims only; 7.2.1 binds only under a declared profile. The Answer lists two relaxations (7.2.1, 8.4) and omits this one. The record therefore misstates what 0.9.0 did to Core.
other_findings.fix: Under 4.2 (b), keep the row and add a note: 'Corrected 2026-10-06: 3.1 (a) covers the basis, not the reasoning or the method; in Core the sentence was a relaxation, not a duplicate. Restored as 3.1 (d) in 0.9.0' (or 'retained as a relaxation', if the editors decide so). Update the Answer's count of relaxations to match.

other_findings.location: 0.9.0 entry, lines 7 and 16, and the Changed list
other_findings.problem: The entry says two requirements were relaxed and migration 'Recommended: nothing', while the table counts the 1.3 evidence-path SHOULD among seven removed SHOULDs without listing it in Changed as a relaxation or a relocation. A reader of the changelog cannot tell that Core stopped recommending a path to reasoning and method.
other_findings.fix: If 3.1 (d) is adopted: list it in Changed as 'Clause 3.1 (d): the recommendation that reasoning and method be reachable or declared unrecorded, carried in 0.8.0 by 1.3, moves to 3.1' and adjust the SHOULD counts. If not adopted: list the removal under Changed as a relaxation, beside 7.2.1 and 8.4, and say under Migration, Recommended, that a page whose answer rests on reasoning kept elsewhere should still point to it.

other_findings.problem: 'Where the method or conditions under which such a fact was established differ from current ones' presupposes that the method was recorded; if it never was, no difference can be seen and the item cannot bind. In Core nothing asks that the method be recorded (corpus 2).
other_findings.fix: No change to 4.3 (b); 3.1 (d) as proposed supplies the missing premise. Add one sentence to the clause-guide row 4.3: 'This presumes the method was written down when the fact was; see 3.1 (d).'

other_findings.problem: 3.1 (a) binds 'material factual claims'; 3.2 (b) binds 'unsupported material claims'. A recommendation or a decided value (corpora 1 and 3) is a material claim but arguably not a factual one, so its only Core protection is 3.2 (b), which a resolving citation satisfies. The two scopes differ by one word with no stated reason.
other_findings.fix: Either drop 'factual' from 3.1 (a) so that the basis requirement reads on every material claim (a MUST widening, breaking under 8.3 (c), so a minor bump with a changelog mark), or leave it and let 3.1 (d) carry recommendations and decisions. The second is the smaller change and is what the proposed rule does.

other_findings.problem: 'A reader may follow the path Index, What, Why, How, Sources from an entry point to an answer and its basis.' Under 0.9.0 Core no clause recommends that an author provide the Why (reasoning) or How (method) legs, so the README describes a path the specification no longer asks anyone to lay. Classification against its canonical source: strengthened. This was also the subtractor's named 'new home' for the removed sentence, and it is a permission to readers, not advice to authors.
other_findings.fix: If 3.1 (d) is adopted the sentence becomes accurate and can stay. Otherwise reword to what Core guarantees: 'from an entry point to an answer and the basis it cites' and drop Why and How from the label, or move the aid to the authoring guide.

other_findings.problem: Refers to 'the evidence path ... (defined in specification section 2)'. The term was defined under Terms in 0.8.0, not section 2, and 0.9.0 removed it; the J-034 guardian noted that dropping the definition leaves this use pointing at nothing (1.4 applied to KADS). The ADR is still 'proposed', so J-034's own unresolved list applies to it.
other_findings.fix: Either mark the ADR superseded or rejected with a pointer to J-034, or reword 'the evidence path' to 'the path from an answer to its reasoning, method, and sources' and delete the parenthetical.

other_findings.problem: 'A material relationship MUST have an explicit meaning ... and a resolvable target' binds only relationships that are stated. A corpus in which two records bear on each other and neither links to the other (corpus 4, D-012 and J-007) violates nothing, so the clause cannot catch a missing relationship, only a mislabeled one. This is probably intentional (a reviewer cannot detect an unstated relation without redoing the work, Contributing question 5), but the clause guide should say so.
other_findings.fix: No normative change. Add to the clause-guide row 7.1.3: 'The rule is about links you write; it does not find links you left out. If a record exists that bears on a decision, cite it under 3.1 (d) or 7.1.5 (c).'
